notes: Anchored corpus for PolyDiff deeplink-family rediscovery + synthetic regressions.
Witnesses are pinned by SHA-256 ONLY. NO payload bytes appear in this repo.

Anchors cover four canonical deeplink divergence shapes: intent_action (MEDIUM-HIGH; Android intent-confusion / implicit-export class), host (MEDIUM; iOS universal-link origin-confusion), host+path or query_params (MEDIUM; deeplink open-redirect class), and path (MEDIUM; custom-scheme traversal class).
Per-case `implementations` lists the two wrapper ids the case is designed to disagree on; the diff engine runs ALL declared wrappers and picks up these axes (plus any others that surface).
Per-case `expected_fact_vector_diff` is keyed by axis name; each value is a 2-element array of the two impls' observations (matches the `implementations` ordering).

cases.summary: An `intent://` URI that, when parsed by Android's Intent.parseUri, produces an Intent with an action that matches a non-declared filter in the SMA's manifest. The Android intent parser emits one action while the SMA's deeplink router resolves a different action from the same URI — leading to silent-export risk (Android intent-confusion bug class). SHA-256-pinned synthetic representation.
cases.limitations: witness bytes are NOT in this repo; pinned-hash anchor only. The expected fact-vector diff documents the canonical disagreement shape — actual parser outputs depend on the pinned wrapper versions.

cases.summary: An HTTPS URL that NSURLComponents parses one way and the SMA's link-handler parses differently. One impl returns the host as the apex domain (origin); the other follows a path-component-as-host quirk that produces a different origin downstream. Maps to iOS universal-link origin-confusion class. SHA-256-pinned synthetic representation.
cases.limitations: synthetic case of our design exercising the host-divergence triage rule; the iOS NSURLComponents quirk class is documented in iOS security guidance generally rather than a specific public bug write-up.

cases.summary: A `signal://` URI with an embedded HTTP URL in a parameter. The proprietary-scheme parser returns the apex host with the embedded URL parked in query_params; a WHATWG-URL fallback that the SMA might call before policy check would resolve to the embedded host directly. If the SMA fetches the parameter without policy check, open-redirect surfaces. Maps to a documented deeplink open-redirect bug class.
cases.limitations: synthetic case of our design exercising the host+path divergence triage rule on a deeplink open-redirect shape. Public bug write-ups for this class are commonly documented in mobile-deeplink security research.

cases.summary: A proprietary-scheme URI (e.g. `sgnl://chat/../..//system/`) where the path component admits traversal. The custom-scheme parser normalizes the traversal segments inconsistently across impls; one resolves to `/system/` while another preserves the literal `chat/../..//system/`. Maps to a deeplink-traversal bug class. SHA-256-pinned synthetic representation.
cases.limitations: synthetic case of our design exercising the path-divergence triage rule on a custom-scheme traversal shape.
